newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to sell CVRD on April 29.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to sell CVRD on April 29.

text.p: Brazil's National Privatization Council on Wednesday set the base price for mining conglomerate Companhia Vale do Rio Doce at 26.67 reais a share or a total of 10.361 billion reais, Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said.
Kandir told reporters that the bid specifications for an initial block sale of 45 percent of voting shares would be published on Thursday, and that the block sale itself would take place on April 29.
Kandir said two independent consultants had recommended minimum prices ranging from 23.2 reais to 25.87 reais per share, but that these were below recent market values.
"(We) determined to have a price that corresponded to recent prices, that is the price of the last 90 days, which turned out to be superior to the prices suggested (by the consultants)," Kandir said.
Kandir said the National Development Bank (BNDES) calculated the average price of CVRD shares over the past 90 days at 26.67 reais a share, giving the company a total value of 10.361 billion reais.
"We decided to accept this proposal from the BNDES as the minimum price which will be published tomorrow," the minister said.
With this minimum price of 26.67 reais per share, the government would raise 3 billion reais in April by selling off a 45 percent stake, Kandir said.
The world's largest exporter of iron ore and a major producer of gold, copper and other metals, the Vale sell-off will be biggest privatization of a Latin American state company to date.

Considered by many a strategic state enterprise, the sale has generated huge controversy and resistance in all sectors of society. To cool nationalist passions, the government has agreed to retain a "golden share" or right of veto in the company.
Last week, the government also decided half the proceeds from the sale of its 51 percent stake would go to an Economic Reconstruction Fund and be used for infrastructure projects.
Earlier on Wednesday, Brazilian stock exchanges suspended trade in Vale stock following a request from the Brazilian Securities and Exchanges Commission.
